topic_summary: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax (MTD IT) affects sole traders and landlords who must use HMRC's new digital Self Assessment system. This menu covers what MTD IT is, how to get started with compliant software, and what to do in the first year after signing up. No verified numeric figures are available for this topic.

terminals.heading: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax may not apply to you
terminals.result_copy: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax applies to sole traders and landlords who file a Self Assessment return. If your only income is employment taxed through PAYE, with no self-employment and no rental property, it does not apply to you and there is nothing you need to do. If that changes — you start a side business, or you begin letting a property — the position changes with it, because MTD follows self-employment and property income. If you are an agent whose question is not covered here, HMRC's guidance for agents is the right starting point.

terminals.heading: Let's narrow down what you need
terminals.result_copy: Your answers do not yet identify which part of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax you need. That is common — it covers several separate things: whether it applies to you and from when, the digital records you must keep, the quarterly updates you send during the year, getting compatible software authorised, and what happens at the end of the year. A short personalised review works out which of these actually affect you and in what order to deal with them.
